newsitem.title: RUSSIA: Yeltsin's wife says planning traditional New Year.
newsitem.headline: Yeltsin's wife says planning traditional New Year.

text.p: President Boris Yeltsin, who had open heart surgery early last month, will go outdoors to greet the New Year in accordance with family tradition, his wife Naina told Russian television in an interview broadcast on Saturday.
"We will greet the New Year in the country. As always, we will go outside just before midnight," Naina said, adding that there would be 10 family members present this year.
The family will gather around a fir tree, exchange presents and drink champagne in the usual way, she said.
Yeltsin, 65, returned to the Kremlin last Monday saying he felt in fine form again after seven weeks spent convalescing from a quintuple heart bypass operation on November 5.

The president, his wife, two daughters and their families are expected to spend the New Year and Christmas holidays at Yeltsin's country residence Gorky 9 outside Moscow. Eastern Orthodox Russians celebrate Christmas on January 6 and 7.
Asked if she had a New Year message for Russians, Naina said: "I would like 1997 to be an easier year for all Russian families."
